result.status: approved 2026-09-29: Seedance for the performance, sync-2-pro for the lips (PLAN.md phase 0c)
findings: Photoreal plates are refused at submission by ByteDance's real-person filter (InputImageSensitiveContentDetected.PrivacyInformation), unbilled. Plates put through a colour print grade (tools/print_grade.py) pass, as ESCAPE VELOCITY's print-graded plates did. Frames Seedance returns are photoreal enough to be refused again, so a cover's start frame needs the same grade.

The mouth follows Seedance's own soundtrack, not our vocal: on the first line of t1g and t3g, lip landmarks (MediaPipe) put the sound 0-60 ms after the mouth for the soundtrack and 210-310 ms before it for our vocal. So avsync.py's soundtrack comparison measures the lip sync.

Seedance starts the speech about 0.5 s into the clip whatever the window's lead-in: our first word is at 0.24 s in t1g-t3g and came at 0.48-0.52 s (the soundtrack 235-300 ms late); in the cover it's at 1.55 s and came at about 0.55 s (1 s early). Within a line the timing then drifts only 25-35 ms. Across the 2.1 s pause the second line shifts again (t1g 300 to 224 ms, t3g 75 ms, t2g not matched).
As placed, all three clips are 0 % in sync; moved earlier by the measured slip they are 71 %, 51 % and 49 %. All come back in colour, with no watermark.

Covers: with frame_images the job is image-to-video and the audio is ignored (cover_g: its own reading of the line, exact start frame, PSNR 32 dB). Without it, '@Image2 as the first frame.' keeps the audio but only lands near the frame (cover_b_g: PSNR 22 dB, a visible jump), and its speech came 1 s early.

The one revision (t1r-t3r, $2.80): single-line 4 s windows with the first word 0.55 s in. Two of the three started on time (+10 and +25 ms at the first word), which bears out the fixed start, but then ran about 10 % slow, reaching +150 to +170 ms by the line's last word; t1r read the line in its own timing and voice and never matched. As placed 0 %, 17 % and 21 % in sync; moved by the measured slip 0 %, 62 % and 64 %.

So Seedance's copy of the vocal can start on time with a 0.5 s lead-in, but inside a line its timing wanders by 25-170 ms, and now and then it re-reads the line: on its own it doesn't hold one frame (42 ms).

The print grade: every graded plate passed the filter and every clip came back in colour, without a watermark. How much print texture survives varies by clip, from visible dots (t1r) to nearly photoreal (t3g, t3r); t2r came out dark and muted.

sync-2-pro on fal ($0.84) redrew the mouth to our vocal on t3g and t2r. On t3g the lips now close on the frames of the /m/ in both 'I'm's and the /b/ of 'job', where Seedance's mouth was still open, and the 'job' opening moved from 1.75 s into the word (1.34-1.62 s). On t2r the /m/ closes on its frame and the /b/ of 'job' one or two frames late. The mouth and teeth come out clean. So Seedance for the performance and sync-2-pro for the lips is a working route.

The texture stays as part of the look (your call). A preview laid the same 5 px CMYK screen over whole clips at a 35 % blend (and at full strength): the clean t3g and the textured t1r and t2g read as one print, with no moire at full resolution or between consecutive frames. At full strength the 8 px screen is too coarse for close-ups.
